title: EDPB sheds light on anonymisation and web scraping for generative AI and adopts final version of guidelines on blockchain

summary.text: At its July 2026 plenary the European Data Protection Board adopted guidelines on anonymisation. Data counts as anonymous only if it passes three criteria: no record isolation, no linkage and no inference, assessed through either a contextual or a simplified approach. The guidelines are open for public consultation until 30 October 2026.

title: Commission publishes new guidance to support timely Cyber Resilience Act implementation

summary.text: The European Commission published non-binding guidance on applying the Cyber Resilience Act, following a consultation earlier in 2026. It addresses the scope for remote data processing solutions and free and open-source software, substantial modification, support periods, reporting and the required security assessment, and includes 67 practical examples aimed partly at microenterprises and SMEs. The page restates that reporting obligations apply from 11 September 2026 and the main obligations from 11 December 2027.

title: Elastic Agent now runs as an OpenTelemetry Collector: Less memory overhead, zero config changes

summary.text: Elastic explained that from version 9.3 its Elastic Agent is built on the Elastic Distribution of OpenTelemetry Collector instead of supervising separate Beats subprocesses. Existing Beats inputs run as receivers inside the OpenTelemetry pipeline, so configurations carry over unchanged, and the agent accepts OTLP data alongside its traditional collection.

title: Prometheus and OpenTelemetry interoperability in 2026: Survey results

summary.text: An OpenTelemetry blog post reported a survey of 81 users of OpenTelemetry for metrics on Prometheus-compatible backends. The share finding the two hard to use together fell from 29 to 10 per cent; Prometheus exporters still lead for infrastructure metrics (72 per cent) while OpenTelemetry SDKs lead for application metrics (65 per cent); 49 per cent mix both styles; and 65 per cent run vanilla components without vendor distributions.
